PullRequest.Title: feat: implementing word wrap indicators
PullRequest.Body:
Adds an opt-in indicator at the end of every soft wrapped line, so a wrap can be told apart from a real line break. Addresses #47855. Off by default. Set `editor.wordWrapIndicator` to `true` to turn it on; it only has an effect while `editor.wordWrap` is enabled. ## How it works ### Rendering Rendering is done by `WordWrapIndicatorOverlay`, a `DynamicViewOverlay` registered on the content overlay layer in `view.ts` alongside the selection and whitespace overlays, so the glyph scrolls with the text. `prepareRender` walks the view lines of the viewport and produces one HTML string per line. A line gets a glyph only when `continuesWithWrappedLine` is set — that is, when it is followed by a soft wrap rather than by a real line break, and is not the last line of the model — and only when the end of its text can actually be measured. The glyph itself is a single `
` holding U+21A9 LEFTWARDS ARROW WITH HOOK, positioned at the `left` reported for the line's `maxColumn` and sized to `getLineHeightForLineNumber`, so lines carrying a custom line height keep the indicator aligned with their text. ### Color `editorWordWrapIndicator.foreground` is a new theme colour that defaults to `editorWhitespace.foreground`, so out of the box the indicator is as muted as rendered whitespace, while themes can still override it on its own. ### Layout The glyph is drawn after the last character of a wrapped view line, which is a problem when the editor wraps to the viewport: the last column ends where the vertical scrollbar begins, so the glyph would be painted underneath it. `EditorLayoutInfoComputer` therefore takes one column off the wrapping column while the indicator is on (`wrappingColumn = viewportColumn - 1`). `viewportColumn` itself is left untouched, so the minimap, which is sized from the same width, is unaffected. `wordWrapColumn` and `bounded` layouts that already wrap short of the viewport are unchanged, since they have spare width for the glyph anyway. ## Known Limitations The indicator is a purely visual affordance and has a few known gaps. It does not handle bidirectional text: the arrow is a fixed U+21A9 anchored at the measured end of the view line and is never mirrored, so on right-to-left or mixed-direction lines it points the wrong way. The column reserved for it in the layout is a blunt approximation — it is one typical halfwidth character wide, which need not match the width the glyph is actually rendered at, and it is taken off whenever the setting is on, even in a file where no line is long enough to wrap. It is also only reserved when the editor wraps to the viewport, so a `wordWrapColumn` layout, or a `bounded` one whose column is at least as wide as the viewport, can still put the glyph underneath the vertical scrollbar. Because it is decoration-only DOM with `pointer-events: none` and no accessible representation, screen reader users get no equivalent cue that a line is soft wrapped, and the indicator does not show up in the minimap. Finally, `ViewDecorationsChangedEvent` carries no line range, so any decoration change repaints the overlay across the whole viewport. ## Other Editors - Visual Studio - Notepad++ - IntelliJ IDEA Word wrap indicator is shown at the beginning of the wrapped line Does not have word wrap indicator: - XCode - Sublime Text --- ## Manual checklist before marking ready for review - [x] Toggle `editor.wordWrapIndicator` live with a wrapped file open: the glyph appears and disappears without needing a reload. - [x] Glyph sits immediately after the last character, with no gap or overlap, at several `editor.fontSize` values and with a proportional font (`editor.fontFamily` set to a non-monospace family). - [x] Correct with variable line heights - [x] Scroll horizontally in a `wordWrapColumn` file: the glyph tracks the text rather than sticking to the viewport. - [x] Interacts sanely with `editor.renderWhitespace: 'all'` — the glyph should not collide with a trailing whitespace dot. - [x] Not selectable and not copied when selecting across a wrapped line (`pointer-events: none` covers hit testing; verify the clipboard). - [x] Inline suggestions / inlay hints / injected text on a wrapped line do not push the glyph to the wrong position. - [x] `editorWordWrapIndicator.foreground` shows up in `workbench.colorCustomizations` IntelliSense and overriding it takes effect. - [x] Legible in Dark+, Light+, and both high contrast themes — the inherited `editorWhitespace.foreground` is deliberately faint, so confirm it is visible enough in HC without being noisy in the default themes. - [x] Accessibility: confirm the glyph is not announced by the screen reader as line content.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added per-visible-line call path and its nested full decoration loop are explicit in the repository, and scrolling/decoration events explicitly invalidate the enabled overlay. The exact frame cost varies with viewport height and decoration density, so severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work and transient ViewLineRenderingData objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each enabled overlay render performs V calls for V visible view lines, and each call derives text direction by scanning the full cached list of D viewport decorations, making the added pass O(V×D) rather than O(V).
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased render-thread CPU/GC pressure and scroll or decoration-update jank in decorated wrapped editors.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no word-wrap-indicator overlay, so scrolling or decoration changes did not add this extra viewport-wide decorated rendering-data pass.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new overlay calls ctx.viewportData.getViewLineRenderingData for every visible line on each invalidation even though it reads only continuesWithWrappedLine.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 108 calls ctx.viewportData.getViewLineRenderingData(lineNumber) inside the new prepareRender viewport loop; this is the line that introduces the repeated decorated-data derivation.
Findings.Title: Use undecorated line data for the viewport-wide indicator pass
Findings.Impact: With wordWrapIndicator enabled, a tall wrapped editor containing many visible decorations (for example search matches, diagnostics, and inline decorations) repeats the viewport-decoration scan once per visible line whenever scrolling or decoration changes trigger rendering; hundreds of visible lines and decorations can therefore produce tens of thousands of checks on a frame and cause dropped frames.
Findings.Evidence: prepareRender loops from viewport start through end and calls _renderLine for every line. Added line 108 invokes ViewportData.getViewLineRenderingData, which delegates to ViewModel.getViewportViewLineRenderingData. Although ViewModelDecorations caches the viewport collection, ViewModel._getViewLineRenderingData calls _getTextDirection(lineNumber, decorations), and _getTextDirection iterates the entire viewport decoration array for every line. The overlay only consumes lineData.continuesWithWrappedLine; IViewModel.getViewLineData exposes that same property without collecting or scanning decorations.
Findings.Recommendation: Read continuesWithWrappedLine from this._context.viewModel.getViewLineData(lineNumber) (or add an equally narrow accessor) so the pass remains O(V) and avoids allocating full rendering data.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, scroll, or update decorations in a wrapped editor with wordWrapIndicator enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The editor's animation-frame render calls ContentViewOverlays.prepareRender, then WordWrapIndicatorOverlay.prepareRender synchronously before DOM rendering can complete.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: V visible view lines after wrapping and D visible model decorations after the shared viewport-decoration collection is built; the introduced rendering-data path performs O(V×D) decoration checks and V transient rendering-data allocations per invalidated pass.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Events are coalesced to at most one scheduled render per editor animation frame, but each editor processes its visible lines serially; side-by-side editors incur separate passes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The viewport decoration collection is cached for the current visible range, but every per-line rendering-data call still scans that cached collection for text direction. The overlay replaces its string array each dirty pass; unchanged per-line HTML can avoid a DOM replacement only after this CPU work has completed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added viewport loop, the cached collection lookup, the nested decoration scan, event invalidation, and animation-frame critical path are all explicit in code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact frame impact depends on viewport height, zoom, decoration density, and the number of visible editor panes; search results, diagnostics, and inline decorations make hundreds of decorations realistic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity repeated CPU work: the overlay needs only continuesWithWrappedLine but requests full decorated rendering data once per visible line.

Scenarios.Scenario: Construct and render editors while the option remains disabled or wrapping is off
Scenarios.CriticalPath: View construction synchronously allocates and registers one lightweight overlay and snapshots a few computed options; prepareRender exits before per-line work whenever the feature is disabled.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of live editor instances and view events; no viewport-line loop runs while disabled.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Construction is synchronous per editor; scheduled editor renders remain animation-frame coalesced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The disabled overlay retains only its options snapshot and a null render result. There is no external cache or repeated per-line work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor and disabled guards are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Workbench layouts can contain several editors, but the marginal object/listener and constant-time event checks are small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression for the default-disabled path; eager allocation is bounded and lightweight.

Scenarios.Scenario: Enable the indicator or resize an editor using viewport word wrapping
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration/layout recomputation changes wrappingColumn, updates the view-line mapping, and schedules the resulting paint before the editor presents the new layout.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Document line count and line lengths control rewrapping; visible wrapped lines control indicator DOM cardinality. Reserving one column can add view lines for content near a wrap boundary.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Configuration and line-mapping updates are serialized on the editor thread; resulting paint is animation-frame coalesced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Changing the effective wrapping column invalidates wrapping/layout state; unchanged subsequent renders reuse normal view-model state, while the indicator keeps only viewport HTML strings.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the rewrap path and one-column change; low concern that it is independently avoidable while preserving the proposed layout behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The cost varies with file size and how many lines lie near exact viewport-width boundaries, but it occurs on explicit enable/resize and is inherent to reserving indicator space.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: this is bounded, intentional layout work rather than an accidental frequency or fan-out regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 13 changed files. Submitted one medium-severity finding for the indicator's O(V×D) decorated-data work on the render critical path; no external I/O boundaries, unbounded retention, concurrency burst, or shipped regression fix was found.
